title: Bolt.new
summary: An AI builder with a documented JavaScript web-app path and an advertised customer-cloud deployment option.

sources.title: Bolt Forge: build with open-source AI models in Bolt

facts.label: Workflow
facts.value: JavaScript web apps; mobile path uses Expo

facts.label: Privacy / data handling
facts.value: The general privacy policy says eligible Bolt AI content may be used for model development and de-identified dataset licensing unless opted out, starting no earlier than 2026-10-07 or a later account Terms date. Forge has separate affirmative consent: its Help Center says prompts, code, project files, configuration, tool calls, edit histories and fix traces may be de-identified and used by partners to train open-source models; EEA, UK and Swiss sessions are excluded. Switching away stops new Forge collection, but already collected data is not automatically removed and may require a deletion request. No account, consent or setting was inspected.

facts.label: Product self-hosting
facts.value: Bolt advertises a BYOK deployment option that can run Bolt in a customer AWS or Azure tenant with isolated compute. The public security page does not detail component scope, architecture, eligibility, inference path or account setup; no account or deployment was inspected.

facts.label: Code / data portability
facts.value: Official documentation provides a GitHub version-control integration.

prices.name: Lite
prices.billing: Monthly; waitlist and access code required
prices.allowance: Forge only; Standard and Max agents are unavailable, and extra Forge usage cannot be purchased on Lite; 2026-10-14 is the last signup day, while existing Lite subscribers can continue after the preview

sections.heading: Check the technology fit
paragraphs: The official introduction describes JavaScript web frameworks and an Expo path for mobile applications. Verify the dependencies and backend requirements of your intended project instead of interpreting that scope as support for every language.

sections.heading: Review the exported project
paragraphs: Use the documented GitHub integration and test a clean checkout. Confirm environment variables, database access and the deployment procedure separately. Token allowances should be evaluated against observed work, not converted into an invented number of finished features.

pros.text: Bolt documents full-stack web apps built with JavaScript-based frameworks and a separate Expo route for mobile apps.
The product documentation describes GitHub version control alongside databases and hosting in Bolt Cloud.
Bolt advertises an option to deploy the platform in a customer AWS or Azure tenant; verify architecture and eligibility before relying on that boundary.

cons.text: The documented full-stack web-app scope is JavaScript-based; confirm support before choosing a project built around another language or framework.
GitHub sync should be rehearsed as a handoff; the integration docs describe repository sync rather than an in-product merge workflow.

The published privacy policy describes prospective model-development and dataset-licensing uses for eligible Bolt AI content. Effective dates, Forge consent, account exclusions and opt-out controls must be checked against the account; none were inspected.

Forge's research preview runs 2026-09-14 through 2026-10-14. Pro's no-extra-cost Forge access ends with the preview; existing Lite subscribers can continue afterward, but 2026-10-14 is the last signup day. Teams and Enterprise are unsupported.

faqs.question: Can Bolt start from an existing repository?
faqs.answer: The official introduction describes importing an existing GitHub repository. Test a clean checkout and its external services before relying on the handoff.

faqs.question: Does its documented web-app path cover every language?
faqs.answer: The documentation describes JavaScript-based web frameworks, so verify the exact framework and dependencies for your project.

faqs.question: Can Bolt use project content to develop AI models?
faqs.answer: The general policy describes prospective model-development and de-identified dataset-licensing uses for eligible Bolt AI content, no earlier than 2026-10-07 or a later account Terms date unless opted out. Forge is separate: its Help Center says first use requires acceptance and describes de-identified prompts, code, project files, configuration, tool calls, edit histories and fix traces being used by partners to train open-source models, with EEA, UK and Swiss sessions excluded. Switching agents stops new Forge collection, but collected material is not automatically deleted; a removal request may be needed. This account's applicable agreement, region, consent and settings were not checked.

faqs.question: Can Bolt itself run in a customer cloud?
faqs.answer: Bolt advertises a BYOK option for running Bolt in a customer AWS or Azure tenant with isolated compute. The public page does not document the component boundary, architecture, eligibility or inference route. No account or deployment was checked.

faqs.question: Does Bolt Forge establish local model inference?
faqs.answer: No. Bolt describes Forge as an open-model agent running on Bolt-reserved hardware, while the agent guide describes model selection behind the scenes and the product article places app execution in browser WebContainers. These pages do not establish a model running on the user device or a customer-selected local endpoint, so local inference remains unverified.

faqs.question: What does Bolt Lite include and cost?
faqs.answer: Bolt lists Lite at USD 9 per month through a waitlist/access-code path. The Forge Help Center says Lite supports Forge only, not Standard or Max agents, and does not allow buying extra Forge usage. October 14, 2026 is the last day to sign up; existing Lite subscribers can continue using Forge after the preview. The general pricing page does not list Lite; no account access or checkout was verified.

faqs.question: Which Bolt plans currently support Forge?
faqs.answer: The Help Center says Forge’s research preview runs from 2026-09-14 through 2026-10-14 and that Forge continues as a working lab afterward. Individual Pro includes Forge at no extra cost only through the preview, then loses Forge access; Teams and Enterprise are unsupported. Lite is USD 9/month through a waitlist/access-code path; October 14, 2026 is the last signup day, while existing Lite subscribers can continue afterward. No account access or plan eligibility was checked.

verdict: Shortlist Bolt for a prototype that fits its documented technology scope. Validate the export and deployment steps before choosing a paid tier.
notFor: Projects assuming every backend language is supported
migration: Rehearse the GitHub handoff, then build from a clean checkout. Inventory database, hosting and secret configuration separately from the code.
gaps: Verify the account's applicable Terms effective date, region, organization-managed status, model-development opt-out and any Bolt Forge consent; no account settings or agreement were inspected.

Confirm eligibility, component scope and operating requirements for customer-cloud BYOK; verify Lite waitlist/account access and the applicable Forge consent, region and data-use controls. No account, agreement, deployment, model endpoint or checkout was inspected.

Bolt Forge documentation does not establish an on-device or customer-selected local inference endpoint; verify the required model route before claiming local inference. No account or endpoint was tested.
